# Complete Language source generators

## Goal

Deliver all 122 generator products and their 36,686 declared cells in one Change.

## Architecture

Specialized C++ generators live in the plugin Framework/Generate and are constructed directly; FCodeGenerator stays empty. Each product owns its source and observations, and generator tests do not compile or execute AS. See [design.md](design.md).

## Global constraints

- Preserve the whole product catalog; batch order does not narrow scope. Existing ForLoop is a baseline, not a new missing class.
- Keep WITH_ANGELSCRIPT_UNITTESTS disabled and use WITH_ANGELSCRIPT_TESTS for replacement tests.
- Run C++ tests through Harness in the selected workspace; no Builder/VM, host runtime registration or full UE suite is needed for source-generation proof.
- Exactly one GeneratesAndExportsAllCases Automation method per generator exports one complete .as dump beside the actual run log; task Cases are checks within that method.
- Case tables and gold must be derived independently of the generator under test. Document limited observations rather than silently treating markers as complete values.
- Commands below run from workspace root in PowerShell 7 after importing Harness and setting $context = New-HarnessContext. Before a proving run, build the selected editor with Harness ue.build (TimeoutMs = 900000) whenever the binary is stale. Require exact discovered case results, not just dispatch success.
- Task 1.1 supplies the shared descriptor header; remaining products consume that value contract.
- Independent product nodes may share test runs with exact task-to-case mapping; shared UE build/test resources remain serialized.
- Execution conventions: [.agents/skills/harness/references/execution-conventions.md](../../../../.agents/skills/harness/references/execution-conventions.md).

## Requirement coverage

| Requirement / acceptance | Tasks |
|---|---|
| Complete initial 122-product inventory and 36,686 cells | Every product below; 14.1 |
| PascalCase names, one test per generator and complete single-file run-local source dumps | 1.1 supplies test I/O helpers; every product performs full export; 14.1 verifies catalog/test mapping |
| Owned consumer descriptors, exact entry lookup, typed outcomes and canonical single-case source | 1.1 defines shared value types; every product implements the APIs; 14.1 proves consumer use |
| Separate compile rejects and runtime faults | Every product with those catalog categories; 14.1 |
| Stable owned source, identities, helper isolation, malformed-input behavior | Every product below |
| Explicit numerical, host and lifecycle observation limits | Operators, Conversions, Functions and Properties product nodes; 14.1 |

Self-review 2026-09-15: every catalog product has one task; acceptance is mapped; placeholder and symbol checks recorded in attachments/data/planning-validation.md.

## [x] 1.1 Verify and complete the ForLoopGenerator source product

Deliver `LANG-CF-FOR-CLAUSES` across all 24 declared cells. Read its [catalog contract](attachments/drafts/findings/cf-products.md#lang-cf-for-clauses) and the common design; normalize documented template defects without removing cells.

**Outcome**

Produce 24 non-reject aggregate entries and 0 separately generated reject cases. Keep the catalog category split and source-only observation boundaries. Retain the assertions from all five existing ForLoop tests inside the single GeneratesAndExportsAllCases method; update the 24-cell gold entry spelling to PascalCase while retaining every generated operation and expected observation.

**Interfaces**

Consumes: `FCodeGenerator` from Framework/Generate/AngelscriptTestCodeGenerator.h:7 and the constructor/oracle routines in `Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/Legacy/AngelScriptSDK/Language/ControlFlow/AngelscriptNativeForClauseTests.cpp` (dormant source evidence, not a runtime dependency). Produces the following interfaces; names come from [glossary](attachments/drafts/glossary.md), the product catalog and the inspected ForLoop header convention.

```cpp
namespace AngelscriptTest::Generate {
struct FForLoopParams; // Product-specific typed axes and FunctionName; only real numeric knobs.
class FForLoopGenerator final : public FCodeGenerator {
public:
    FStringView GetProductId() const;
    TArray<FGeneratedCaseInfo> ListCases() const;
    FString BuildCaseSource(FStringView CaseId) const;
    FString BuildDumpSource() const;
    FString BuildAllSource(int32& OutCaseCount) const;
    FString BuildForSource(const FForLoopParams& Params) const;
    int32 GetExpected(FStringView CaseId) const;
};
}
```

This task owns `AngelscriptTest::FGeneratedCaseExport` and its ResolveOutputFile and WriteDump signatures fixed in design.md; it proves the test-only export helper inside the single ForLoop method.

This task also produces `AngelscriptTestGeneratedCase.h`, `EGeneratedCaseOutcome`, `EGeneratedCaseExecution` and `FGeneratedCaseInfo` exactly as specified in design.md Consumer case enumeration; it proves that shared contract through the existing ForLoop product.

```cpp
namespace AngelscriptTest::Generate
{
enum class EGeneratedCaseOutcome : uint8
{
    ReturnValue,
    CompileReject,
    RuntimeException,
};

enum class EGeneratedCaseExecution : uint8
{
    Standalone,
    RequiresHostSetup,
    SourceOnly,
};

struct FGeneratedCaseInfo
{
    FString CaseId;
    FString EntryDeclaration;
    EGeneratedCaseOutcome Outcome = EGeneratedCaseOutcome::ReturnValue;
    EGeneratedCaseExecution Execution = EGeneratedCaseExecution::SourceOnly;
    TOptional<int32> ExpectedReturn;
    FString ExpectedException;
    bool bLimitedObservation = false;
    FString ExecutionNotes;
};
}
```

Register exactly one `TEST_METHOD(GeneratesAndExportsAllCases)`; all Cases below are checks within it. Test class identity: `Angelscript.UnitTest.Framework.ForLoopGenerator`. Each documented axis becomes a product-specific typed field; use the catalog token order and existing first-batch names where already settled.

**Cases**

1. **Complete cell partition** — existing control
   Given the catalog axis tables, when all cells are generated, then exactly 24 distinct IDs exist, with 24 aggregate entries and 0 reject IDs. Oracle: independently enumerated literal axes and the declared category partition; check complete expected ID set and order, not only total count.
2. **Identity and owned source** — new RED
   Given catalog member `LANG-CF-FOR-CLAUSES-PRESENT-OMITTED-PRESENT-ONE`, when its appropriate normal/fault or reject source is generated and retained across another call, then the original text is unchanged and its entry corresponds to that ID. Repeated aggregate generation must be byte-identical. For a single normal case, empty FunctionName means `Entry`; `ProbeEntry` changes only the requested entry identity. Reject-only products check their reject builder instead.
3. **Independent source and observation proof** — new RED
   Given every normal cell and the cited source constructor/oracle, then GetExpected matches an independently derived table across the declared observation domain. Compare reviewed representative gold for every distinct source-construction branch and category. Check operation text and typed operands so a constant expected answer cannot substitute for the generated operation. For rejection/fault cells, verify source trigger and category rather than a normal-return integer.
4. **Isolation and invalid inputs** — new RED
   Given repeated entries with case-dependent types/helpers/state, then generated definitions do not collide and cases cannot inherit prior mutable initialization. Given `UNKNOWN-CASE`, an out-of-domain enum cast or FunctionName `bad-name`, new-product source APIs return empty with no partial module; positive-only builders reject reject-category inputs. Test unknown GetExpected separately as zero fallback, never as membership proof. Preserve established baseline behavior where the design explicitly exempts it.

5. **Complete consumer descriptors** — new RED
   Call ListCases and compare its exact ordered IDs and category membership against the independent product case table. For each non-reject row, EntryDeclaration exactly names its aggregate and BuildCaseSource entry; every reject has no callable declaration and an isolated nonempty source. The non-reject projection equals OutCaseCount; the reject projection equals ListRejectCaseIds where supported. No test discovers the expected ID set by parsing the generator output.
6. **Owned typed expectations and direct replay** — new RED
   Every executable ReturnValue row has ExpectedReturn set and matching the independently derived int32 observation; runtime exceptions carry exact text and no integer value; compile rejects have neither. Apply the design's explicit host/source-only/limited-observation rules. Retain and modify one returned list, then enumerate again and verify original identities/expectations. BuildCaseSource for UNKNOWN-CASE and a foreign product ID returns empty. A real expected zero remains a populated optional and cannot be confused with an unknown ID.

7. **One complete readable source dump** — new RED
   BuildDumpSource contains exactly 24 case-section markers covering the independent expected ID set: non-reject entries in one aggregate section, and reject modules in separately labeled units when applicable. Common aggregate helpers occur once; every body's canonical source meaning matches the existing source APIs. Write one <ClassWithoutF>.as file under GeneratedCases beside this run's actual Unreal.log, then compare UTF-8-without-BOM readback with the exact returned text. Do not create per-case files, product subdirectories or index.json.
8. **Stable layout and retained failure artifact** — new RED
   Independently authored representative gold checks PascalCase entries, LF plus final newline, tab indentation, Allman braces, one statement per line, one blank line between top-level functions and no trailing whitespace. Call the generator twice and require byte equality. Attempt the product dump write before aborting assertions, so a later assertion failure retains it. A probe targeting a regular-file directory or invalid path must return a write error rather than success and must not touch sibling dumps. Log the exact product path and case count, not the complete source.

**Files**

```diff
+Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/FrameworkTests/Generate/GeneratedCaseExport.h
+Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/FrameworkTests/Generate/GeneratedCaseExport.cpp
 Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/FrameworkTests/Gold/ForLoopAllSource.as
+Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/Framework/Generate/AngelscriptTestGeneratedCase.h
 Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/Framework/Generate/AngelscriptTestForLoopGenerator.h
 Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/Framework/Generate/AngelscriptTestForLoopGenerator.cpp
-Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/FrameworkTests/GenerateTests.cpp
+Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/FrameworkTests/Generate/ForLoopGeneratorTests.cpp
+Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/FrameworkTests/Gold/LanguageGenerators/ForLoopGenerator/RepresentativeSources.as
+AngelscriptTestCode/Generators/cf/LANG-CF-FOR-CLAUSES.md
```

Gold directory ownership is limited to this product; keep representative sources only. The rule document records exact axes, source branches, categories, observation formulas and host/lifecycle limits. It is an author reference excluded from the ordinary .as projection.

**Verification**

```powershell
Invoke-Harness -Command ue.test -Context $context -Parameters @{ TestPrefix = 'Angelscript.UnitTest.Framework.ForLoopGenerator.GeneratesAndExportsAllCases'; Fast = $true; TimeoutMs = 600000 }
```

All named cases must execute and pass with a current C++ binary. Record generated-source proof separately from language-runtime proof, which is out of scope.

Register exactly one `TEST_METHOD(GeneratesAndExportsAllCases)`; all Cases below are checks within it. Test class identity: `Angelscript.UnitTest.Framework.Generate.NestedTargetGenerator`. Each documented axis becomes a product-specific typed field; use the catalog token order and existing first-batch names where already settled.

**Cases**

1. **Complete cell partition** — new RED
   Given the catalog axis tables, when all cells are generated, then exactly 18 distinct IDs exist, with 18 aggregate entries and 0 reject IDs. Oracle: independently enumerated literal axes and the declared category partition; check complete expected ID set and order, not only total count.
2. **Identity and owned source** — new RED
   Given catalog member `LANG-CF-NESTED-TARGETS-NESTED_LOOP-BREAK-INNER`, when its appropriate normal/fault or reject source is generated and retained across another call, then the original text is unchanged and its entry corresponds to that ID. Repeated aggregate generation must be byte-identical. For a single normal case, empty FunctionName means `Entry`; `ProbeEntry` changes only the requested entry identity. Reject-only products check their reject builder instead.
3. **Independent source and observation proof** — new RED
   Given every normal cell and the cited source constructor/oracle, then GetExpected matches an independently derived table across the declared observation domain. Compare reviewed representative gold for every distinct source-construction branch and category. Check operation text and typed operands so a constant expected answer cannot substitute for the generated operation. For rejection/fault cells, verify source trigger and category rather than a normal-return integer.
4. **Isolation and invalid inputs** — new RED
   Given repeated entries with case-dependent types/helpers/state, then generated definitions do not collide and cases cannot inherit prior mutable initialization. Given `UNKNOWN-CASE`, an out-of-domain enum cast or FunctionName `bad-name`, new-product source APIs return empty with no partial module; positive-only builders reject reject-category inputs. Test unknown GetExpected separately as zero fallback, never as membership proof. Preserve established baseline behavior where the design explicitly exempts it.

5. **Complete consumer descriptors** — new RED
   Call ListCases and compare its exact ordered IDs and category membership against the independent product case table. For each non-reject row, EntryDeclaration exactly names its aggregate and BuildCaseSource entry; every reject has no callable declaration and an isolated nonempty source. The non-reject projection equals OutCaseCount; the reject projection equals ListRejectCaseIds where supported. No test discovers the expected ID set by parsing the generator output.
6. **Owned typed expectations and direct replay** — new RED
   Every executable ReturnValue row has ExpectedReturn set and matching the independently derived int32 observation; runtime exceptions carry exact text and no integer value; compile rejects have neither. Apply the design's explicit host/source-only/limited-observation rules. Retain and modify one returned list, then enumerate again and verify original identities/expectations. BuildCaseSource for UNKNOWN-CASE and a foreign product ID returns empty. A real expected zero remains a populated optional and cannot be confused with an unknown ID.

7. **One complete readable source dump** — new RED
   BuildDumpSource contains exactly 18 case-section markers covering the independent expected ID set: non-reject entries in one aggregate section, and reject modules in separately labeled units when applicable. Common aggregate helpers occur once; every body's canonical source meaning matches the existing source APIs. Write one <ClassWithoutF>.as file under GeneratedCases beside this run's actual Unreal.log, then compare UTF-8-without-BOM readback with the exact returned text. Do not create per-case files, product subdirectories or index.json.
8. **Stable layout and retained failure artifact** — new RED
   Independently authored representative gold checks PascalCase entries, LF plus final newline, tab indentation, Allman braces, one statement per line, one blank line between top-level functions and no trailing whitespace. Call the generator twice and require byte equality. Attempt the product dump write before aborting assertions, so a later assertion failure retains it. A probe targeting a regular-file directory or invalid path must return a write error rather than success and must not touch sibling dumps. Log the exact product path and case count, not the complete source.

**Interfaces**

Consumes `FGeneratedCaseInfo`, `EGeneratedCaseOutcome` and `EGeneratedCaseExecution` from task 1.1 (Framework/Generate/AngelscriptTestGeneratedCase.h). Consumes: `FCodeGenerator` from Framework/Generate/AngelscriptTestCodeGenerator.h:7 and the constructor/oracle routines in `Plugins/Angelscript/Source/AngelscriptTest/Legacy/AngelScriptSDK/Language/Expressions/AngelscriptNativeExpressionChainTests.cpp` (dormant source evidence, not a runtime dependency). Produces the following interfaces; names come from [glossary](attachments/drafts/glossary.md), the product catalog and the inspected ForLoop header convention.

```cpp
namespace AngelscriptTest::Generate {
struct FExprChainParams; // Product-specific typed axes and FunctionName; only real numeric knobs.
class FExprChainGenerator final : public FCodeGenerator {
public:

    TArray<FGeneratedCaseInfo> ListCases() const;
    FString BuildCaseSource(FStringView CaseId) const;
    FString BuildDumpSource() const;
    FString BuildAllSource(int32& OutCaseCount) const;
    FString BuildExpressionChainSource(const FExprChainParams& Params) const;
    int32 GetExpected(FStringView CaseId) const;

    TArray<FString> ListRejectCaseIds() const;
};
```

Register exactly one `TEST_METHOD(GeneratesAndExportsAllCases)`; all Cases below are checks within it. Test class identity: `Angelscript.UnitTest.Framework.Generate.ExprChainGenerator`. Each documented axis becomes a product-specific typed field; use the catalog token order and existing first-batch names where already settled.

**Cases**

1. **Complete cell partition** — new RED
   Given the catalog axis tables, when all cells are generated, then exactly 800 distinct IDs exist, with 480 aggregate entries and 320 reject IDs. Oracle: independently enumerated literal axes and the declared category partition; check complete expected ID set and order, not only total count.
2. **Identity and owned source** — new RED
   Given catalog member `LANG-EXPR-CHAIN-INITIALIZER-TWO-CALL_MEMBER-VALID`, when its appropriate normal/fault or reject source is generated and retained across another call, then the original text is unchanged and its entry corresponds to that ID. Repeated aggregate generation must be byte-identical. For a single normal case, empty FunctionName means `Entry`; `ProbeEntry` changes only the requested entry identity. Reject-only products check their reject builder instead.
3. **Independent source and observation proof** — new RED
   Given every normal cell and the cited source constructor/oracle, then GetExpected matches an independently derived table across the declared observation domain. Compare reviewed representative gold for every distinct source-construction branch and category. Check operation text and typed operands so a constant expected answer cannot substitute for the generated operation. For rejection/fault cells, verify source trigger and category rather than a normal-return integer.
4. **Isolation and invalid inputs** — new RED
   Given repeated entries with case-dependent types/helpers/state, then generated definitions do not collide and cases cannot inherit prior mutable initialization. Given `UNKNOWN-CASE`, an out-of-domain enum cast or FunctionName `bad-name`, new-product source APIs return empty with no partial module; positive-only builders reject reject-category inputs. Test unknown GetExpected separately as zero fallback, never as membership proof. Preserve established baseline behavior where the design explicitly exempts it.

5. **Complete consumer descriptors** — new RED
   Call ListCases and compare its exact ordered IDs and category membership against the independent product case table. For each non-reject row, EntryDeclaration exactly names its aggregate and BuildCaseSource entry; every reject has no callable declaration and an isolated nonempty source. The non-reject projection equals OutCaseCount; the reject projection equals ListRejectCaseIds where supported. No test discovers the expected ID set by parsing the generator output.
6. **Owned typed expectations and direct replay** — new RED
   Every executable ReturnValue row has ExpectedReturn set and matching the independently derived int32 observation; runtime exceptions carry exact text and no integer value; compile rejects have neither. Apply the design's explicit host/source-only/limited-observation rules. Retain and modify one returned list, then enumerate again and verify original identities/expectations. BuildCaseSource for UNKNOWN-CASE and a foreign product ID returns empty. A real expected zero remains a populated optional and cannot be confused with an unknown ID.

7. **One complete readable source dump** — new RED
   BuildDumpSource contains exactly 800 case-section markers covering the independent expected ID set: non-reject entries in one aggregate section, and reject modules in separately labeled units when applicable. Common aggregate helpers occur once; every body's canonical source meaning matches the existing source APIs. Write one <ClassWithoutF>.as file under GeneratedCases beside this run's actual Unreal.log, then compare UTF-8-without-BOM readback with the exact returned text. Do not create per-case files, product subdirectories or index.json.
8. **Stable layout and retained failure artifact** — new RED
   Independently authored representative gold checks PascalCase entries, LF plus final newline, tab indentation, Allman braces, one statement per line, one blank line between top-level functions and no trailing whitespace. Call the generator twice and require byte equality. Attempt the product dump write before aborting assertions, so a later assertion failure retains it. A probe targeting a regular-file directory or invalid path must return a write error rather than success and must not touch sibling dumps. Log the exact product path and case count, not the complete source.

Register exactly one `TEST_METHOD(GeneratesAndExportsAllCases)`; all Cases below are checks within it. Test class identity: `Angelscript.UnitTest.Framework.Generate.FnOverloadGenerator`. Each documented axis becomes a product-specific typed field; use the catalog token order and existing first-batch names where already settled.

**Cases**

1. **Complete cell partition** — new RED
   Given the catalog axis tables, when all cells are generated, then exactly 28 distinct IDs exist, with 14 aggregate entries and 14 reject IDs. Oracle: independently enumerated literal axes and the declared category partition; check complete expected ID set and order, not only total count.
2. **Identity and owned source** — new RED
   Given catalog member `LANG-FN-OVERLOAD-TYPE-EXACT`, when its appropriate normal/fault or reject source is generated and retained across another call, then the original text is unchanged and its entry corresponds to that ID. Repeated aggregate generation must be byte-identical. For a single normal case, empty FunctionName means `Entry`; `ProbeEntry` changes only the requested entry identity. Reject-only products check their reject builder instead.
3. **Independent source and observation proof** — new RED
   Given every normal cell and the cited source constructor/oracle, then GetExpected matches an independently derived table across the declared observation domain. Compare reviewed representative gold for every distinct source-construction branch and category. Check operation text and typed operands so a constant expected answer cannot substitute for the generated operation. For rejection/fault cells, verify source trigger and category rather than a normal-return integer.
4. **Isolation and invalid inputs** — new RED
   Given repeated entries with case-dependent types/helpers/state, then generated definitions do not collide and cases cannot inherit prior mutable initialization. Given `UNKNOWN-CASE`, an out-of-domain enum cast or FunctionName `bad-name`, new-product source APIs return empty with no partial module; positive-only builders reject reject-category inputs. Test unknown GetExpected separately as zero fallback, never as membership proof. Preserve established baseline behavior where the design explicitly exempts it.

5. **Complete consumer descriptors** — new RED
   Call ListCases and compare its exact ordered IDs and category membership against the independent product case table. For each non-reject row, EntryDeclaration exactly names its aggregate and BuildCaseSource entry; every reject has no callable declaration and an isolated nonempty source. The non-reject projection equals OutCaseCount; the reject projection equals ListRejectCaseIds where supported. No test discovers the expected ID set by parsing the generator output.
6. **Owned typed expectations and direct replay** — new RED
   Every executable ReturnValue row has ExpectedReturn set and matching the independently derived int32 observation; runtime exceptions carry exact text and no integer value; compile rejects have neither. Apply the design's explicit host/source-only/limited-observation rules. Retain and modify one returned list, then enumerate again and verify original identities/expectations. BuildCaseSource for UNKNOWN-CASE and a foreign product ID returns empty. A real expected zero remains a populated optional and cannot be confused with an unknown ID.

7. **One complete readable source dump** — new RED
   BuildDumpSource contains exactly 28 case-section markers covering the independent expected ID set: non-reject entries in one aggregate section, and reject modules in separately labeled units when applicable. Common aggregate helpers occur once; every body's canonical source meaning matches the existing source APIs. Write one <ClassWithoutF>.as file under GeneratedCases beside this run's actual Unreal.log, then compare UTF-8-without-BOM readback with the exact returned text. Do not create per-case files, product subdirectories or index.json.
8. **Stable layout and retained failure artifact** — new RED
   Independently authored representative gold checks PascalCase entries, LF plus final newline, tab indentation, Allman braces, one statement per line, one blank line between top-level functions and no trailing whitespace. Call the generator twice and require byte equality. Attempt the product dump write before aborting assertions, so a later assertion failure retains it. Register exactly one `TEST_METHOD(GeneratesAndExportsAllCases)`; all Cases below are checks within it. Test class identity: `Angelscript.UnitTest.Framework.Generate.FnReturnGenerator`. Each documented axis becomes a product-specific typed field; use the catalog token order and existing first-batch names where already settled.

**Cases**

1. **Complete cell partition** — new RED
   Given the catalog axis tables, when all cells are generated, then exactly 136 distinct IDs exist, with 103 aggregate entries and 33 reject IDs. Oracle: independently enumerated literal axes and the declared category partition; check complete expected ID set and order, not only total count.
2. **Identity and owned source** — new RED
   Given catalog member `LANG-FN-RETURN-DIRECT-VOID`, when its appropriate normal/fault or reject source is generated and retained across another call, then the original text is unchanged and its entry corresponds to that ID. Repeated aggregate generation must be byte-identical. For a single normal case, empty FunctionName means `Entry`; `ProbeEntry` changes only the requested entry identity. Reject-only products check their reject builder instead.
3. **Independent source and observation proof** — new RED
   Given every normal cell and the cited source constructor/oracle, then GetExpected matches an independently derived table across the declared observation domain. Compare reviewed representative gold for every distinct source-construction branch and category. Check operation text and typed operands so a constant expected answer cannot substitute for the generated operation. For rejection/fault cells, verify source trigger and category rather than a normal-return integer.
4. **Isolation and invalid inputs** — new RED
   Given repeated entries with case-dependent types/helpers/state, then generated definitions do not collide and cases cannot inherit prior mutable initialization. Given `UNKNOWN-CASE`, an out-of-domain enum cast or FunctionName `bad-name`, new-product source APIs return empty with no partial module; positive-only builders reject reject-category inputs. Test unknown GetExpected separately as zero fallback, never as membership proof. Preserve established baseline behavior where the design explicitly exempts it.

5. **Complete consumer descriptors** — new RED
   Call ListCases and compare its exact ordered IDs and category membership against the independent product case table. For each non-reject row, EntryDeclaration exactly names its aggregate and BuildCaseSource entry; every reject has no callable declaration and an isolated nonempty source. The non-reject projection equals OutCaseCount; the reject projection equals ListRejectCaseIds where supported. No test discovers the expected ID set by parsing the generator output.
6. **Owned typed expectations and direct replay** — new RED
   Every executable ReturnValue row has ExpectedReturn set and matching the independently derived int32 observation; runtime exceptions carry exact text and no integer value; compile rejects have neither. Apply the design's explicit host/source-only/limited-observation rules. Retain and modify one returned list, then enumerate again and verify original identities/expectations. BuildCaseSource for UNKNOWN-CASE and a foreign product ID returns empty. A real expected zero remains a populated optional and cannot be confused with an unknown ID.

7. **One complete readable source dump** — new RED
   BuildDumpSource contains exactly 136 case-section markers covering the independent expected ID set: non-reject entries in one aggregate section, and reject modules in separately labeled units when applicable. Common aggregate helpers occur once; every body's canonical source meaning matches the existing source APIs. Write one <ClassWithoutF>.as file under GeneratedCases beside this run's actual Unreal.log, then compare UTF-8-without-BOM readback with the exact returned text. Do not create per-case files, product subdirectories or index.json.
8. **Stable layout and retained failure artifact** — new RED
   Independently authored representative gold checks PascalCase entries, LF plus final newline, tab indentation, Allman braces, one statement per line, one blank line between top-level functions and no trailing whitespace. Call the generator twice and require byte equality. Attempt the product dump write before aborting assertions, so a later assertion failure retains it.
